title: ruby: one helper pulled out of two callers that held the same lines: an extract from each
ruby: a helper whose last statement is a loop, called as a statement: its tail moved, it is no value
old:
class Relations < Source
  def start
    target.start(:db)
    rom = target["db.rom"]
    rom.relations.each do |name, _|
      register(name) { rom.relations[name] }
    end
  end
end
new:
class Relations < Source
  def start
    target.start(:db)
    register_relations target["db.rom"]
  end

  private

  def register_relations(rom)
    rom.relations.each do |name, _|
      register name, rom.relations[name]
    end
  end
end

title: ruby: the callers keep their repeated lines and also call a new helper holding the same lines: a copy, no extract

title: ruby: a one-word helper called as a statement, whose only line the caller lost: too little to be evidence
old:
class Job
  def finish
    flush
    close
  end
end
new:
class Job
  def finish
    flush
    shutdown
  end

  def shutdown
    close
  end
end

title: ruby: the call took the place of an edited expression in an otherwise unchanged line: the helper came from there
old:
class CommonLogger
  def log(env, status, began_at)
    msg = [
      ip:     env[REMOTE_ADDR],
      path:   env[SCRIPT_NAME] + env[PATH_INFO],
      params: env[QUERY_HASH].merge(env[FORM_HASH] || Hash[]),
      status: status
    ]
    logger.info(msg)
  end
end
new:
class CommonLogger
  def log(env, status, began_at)
    msg = [
      ip:     env[REMOTE_ADDR],
      path:   env[SCRIPT_NAME] + env[PATH_INFO],
      params: extract_params(env),
      status: status
    ]
    logger.info(msg)
  end

  def extract_params(env)
    (env[QUERY_HASH] || {}).merge(env[FORM_HASH] || {})
  end
end

title: ruby: the call took the place of an expression that calls other methods (name.strip vs nickname.downcase): not where the helper came from
old:
class Greeter
  def greet(user)
    name = user.name.strip
    "Hello, #{name}"
  end
end
new:
class Greeter
  def greet(user)
    name = display_name(user)
    "Hello, #{name}"
  end

  def display_name(user)
    user.nickname.downcase
  end
end

title: ruby: the call took the place of a lookalike with other symbols (fetch(:timeout) vs fetch(:retries)): not where the helper came from
old:
class Client
  def connect
    timeout = config.fetch(:timeout, 30) + 5
    open(timeout)
  end
end
new:
class Client
  def connect
    timeout = default_timeout + 5
    open(timeout)
  end

  def default_timeout
    config.fetch(:retries, 3)
  end
end

title: ruby: a helper called as a statement whose last line is the edited call it replaced (rake display_cause_details): when the tail does not pair as a statement, it is read as the value, and the extract stays
old:
class Application
  def display_exception_details(ex)
    seen = Thread.current[:seen] ||= []
    return if seen.include? ex
    seen << ex

    display_exception_message_details(ex)
    display_exception_backtrace(ex)
    display_exception_details(ex.cause) if has_cause?(ex)
  end
end
new:
class Application
  def display_exception_details(ex)
    seen << ex

    display_exception_message_details(ex)
    display_exception_backtrace(ex)
    display_cause_details(ex.cause) if has_cause?(ex)
  end

  def display_cause_details(ex)
    return if seen.include? ex

    trace "\nCaused by:"
    display_exception_details(ex)
  end
end
